result.summary:
Read the new test at test/letflow/plugs/cors_test.exs:193-212 directly. It matches CODE-DESIGNER's step-02 design exactly: single combined OPTIONS /api/v1/anything preflight, access-control-request-headers: "x-bpm-user-id, if-match, idempotency-key" (fix_direction's literal exemplar first, other two audited headers alongside), asserts conn.status == 204, then splits the single access-control-allow-headers response value on ", " and asserts membership (`in`) of all three header names individually -- not full-string equality, and not a single-header check. Placed in the existing 'AC3: preflight OPTIONS request, matched origin' describe block immediately after the pinned exact-string assertion test, per design. No other test in the file was altered by this addition (the pre-existing pinned assertion at line 187-188 already reads the corrected 5-header value, which is ELIXIR-DEV/REVIEWER's prior work, out of this gate's scope).

INDEPENDENT PASS-SIDE REPRODUCTION (this branch, post-fix): ran `MIX_ENV=test mix test test/letflow/plugs/cors_test.exs` myself. Real output: `Finished in 0.1 seconds (0.00s async, 0.1s sync)` / `Result: 19 passed`. All 19 tests green, including the new regression test.

INDEPENDENT FAIL-SIDE REPRODUCTION (own throwaway worktree, not TEST-DESIGNER's): created `git worktree add ../letflow-tdv-iss0780-prefix 2ed97a50` myself. Verified before editing that the worktree's lib/letflow/plugs/cors.ex still had the pre-fix `@allow_headers "authorization, content-type"` (grep confirmed, untouched). Inserted only the new test function (byte-identical to the one on this branch) into that worktree's test/letflow/plugs/cors_test.exs, touching nothing in lib/. Linked deps/_build into the worktree via temporary Windows directory junctions (borrowed from the main checkout) to run mix test without a fresh deps fetch, then removed both junctions (`cmd /c rmdir deps`, `cmd /c rmdir _build` -- verified gone) before removing the worktree. Ran `MIX_ENV=test mix test test/letflow/plugs/cors_test.exs` there. Real failing output:

  1) test AC3: preflight OPTIONS request, matched origin ISS-0780 regression: x-bpm-user-id, if-match, and idempotency-key are all allowed on preflight (Letflow.Plugs.CorsTest)
     test/letflow/plugs/cors_test.exs:193
     Assertion with in failed
     code:  assert "x-bpm-user-id" in allowed
     left:  "x-bpm-user-id"
     right: ["authorization", "content-type"]
     stacktrace:
       test/letflow/plugs/cors_test.exs:209: (test)

  Result: 18/19 passed
  Failed: 1 test

This matches TEST-DESIGNER's claimed output exactly (same failing assertion, same right-hand list, same 18/19 count) -- independently confirmed, not copied. Removed the worktree afterward (`git worktree remove --force ../letflow-tdv-iss0780-prefix`); `git worktree list` no longer shows it, and `git status --porcelain` on the main checkout shows no residue from this validation (only a pre-existing unrelated untracked `web/tests/e2e/.pipeline-state/` dir, not touched by this gate).

COVERAGE CHECK: all three added headers (x-bpm-user-id, if-match, idempotency-key) are individually asserted via separate `assert "<name>" in allowed` lines -- not just the fix_direction literal exemplar (x-bpm-user-id) in isolation. No gap.

SCOPE CHECK: `git show --stat d71d761e` shows exactly two files changed -- test/letflow/plugs/cors_test.exs (+21) and handoffs/WF03-ISS0780-20260922/step-04-test-designer.json (+57). lib/letflow/plugs/cors.ex is untouched by this commit, consistent with the fix already being in 3d1bb946.

No skip tags, no TODO-implement placeholders, no shared hardcoded state dependency (each test builds its own conn via Plug.Test, no fixtures shared across tests), tests are self-sufficient (no ordering dependency -- async: false is file-level, not because tests depend on each other's side effects; the one stateful test, the Application.put_env override test, uses on_exit/1 to restore state and does not affect this new test). No hardcoded secrets/connection strings.

All five acceptance criteria met. Gate: PASS.
